dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Deploy a resource by using an ARM template or Bicep file
domanda: A release engineer at Contoso deploys an ARM template to a resource group by running New-AzResourceGroupDeployment without including the -Mode parameter. Which deployment mode does Azure Resource Manager use for this deployment?
opzione_d: Complete, but only if the template defines every resource that already exists in the resource group
spiegazione: Correct: Incremental. The Learn documentation states plainly that "The default mode is incremental." When -Mode is omitted, Resource Manager adds or updates the resources defined in the template and leaves untouched any resource that exists in the resource group but is not in the template. Why the others are wrong: (a) Complete is never the default; it must be requested explicitly with -Mode Complete (PowerShell) or --mode Complete (Azure CLI), because it deletes resources that are absent from the template. (c) Validate is not a deployment mode. Validation is a separate operation (Test-AzResourceGroupDeployment / az deployment group validate); the only two deployment modes are Incremental and Complete. (d) This describes a conditional behaviour that does not exist. Mode selection is an explicit parameter of the deployment operation and is never inferred from the template contents.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Deploy a resource by using an ARM template or Bicep file
domanda: Resource group RG1 currently contains three resources named ResourceA, ResourceB and ResourceC. An ARM template named Template1 defines ResourceA, ResourceB and ResourceD. Template1 is deployed to RG1 by using complete mode. Which resources exist in RG1 after the deployment succeeds?
spiegazione: Correct: ResourceA, ResourceB and ResourceD only. In complete mode, Resource Manager deletes resources that exist in the resource group but aren't specified in the template. ResourceC is not in Template1, so it is deleted. ResourceA and ResourceB are in the template and are redeployed/updated, and ResourceD is created because Resource Manager still tries to create all resources specified in the template in both modes. Why the others are wrong: (b) is the result of an incremental deployment: incremental leaves ResourceC unchanged, so all four would remain. This is the classic distractor. (c) incorrectly assumes complete mode also skips resources that are new in the template; complete mode still creates ResourceD. (d) incorrectly assumes complete mode deletes and recreates everything from scratch. Existing resources whose settings are unchanged have no operation taken against them; they are not deleted and recreated.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
domanda: A virtual network named VNet1 was deployed from an ARM template and later had a tag named Owner with the value "Team A" added to it in the Azure portal. A colleague edits the original template to change the address prefix, but the template's virtual network resource contains no tags element. The colleague redeploys the template to the same resource group by using incremental mode. What happens to the Owner tag on VNet1?
opzione_a: The Owner tag is removed, because properties that aren't included in the template are reset to their default values.
opzione_b: The Owner tag is preserved, because incremental mode only adds or changes the properties that are specified in the template.
opzione_c: The Owner tag is preserved, because tags are metadata and are never evaluated by Azure Resource Manager during a deployment.
opzione_d: The deployment fails with a conflict error because the deployed resource contains a tag that the template does not declare.
spiegazione: Correct: The Owner tag is removed. Microsoft Learn explicitly calls this out as a common misunderstanding: "When redeploying an existing resource in incremental mode, all properties are reapplied. The properties aren't incrementally added... If you don't specify certain properties, Resource Manager interprets the deployment as overwriting those values. Properties that aren't included in the template are reset to the default values." The resource definition in the template always represents the final state of the resource, not a partial update. Why the others are wrong: (b) is exactly the misconception the documentation warns against. "Incremental" refers to how Resource Manager treats resources not in the template, not properties not in the template. (c) is false; tags are part of the resource definition submitted to the resource provider, and the what-if operation reports removed tags as deletions. (d) is false; there is no conflict error for undeclared tags. The deployment succeeds and silently overwrites the tag collection. To keep the tag, the colleague must add it to the template or specify it inline.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Interpret an ARM template or Bicep file
domanda: While reviewing a Bicep file, you notice that it does not contain a targetScope statement. Which scope will the file be deployed at?
spiegazione: Correct: resourceGroup. The Bicep file structure documentation states: "The default target scope is resourceGroup. If you deploy at the resource group level, you don't need to set the target scope in your Bicep file." The four allowed values are resourceGroup, subscription, managementGroup and tenant. Why the others are wrong: (a) subscription must be declared explicitly with targetScope = 'subscription' and is used for subscription-level deployments such as creating resource groups or assigning policies. (b) managementGroup must be declared explicitly and is used for management group deployments. (d) tenant must be declared explicitly and is used for tenant-level deployments. All three are valid values, but none of them is the default.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Interpret an ARM template or Bicep file
domanda: An ARM JSON template that does not use symbolic names deploys an Azure CDN endpoint and a web app. The endpoint must read the first host name of the web app into its originHostHeader property, and the endpoint must be deployed only after the web app. The template author wants to rely on an implicit dependency instead of adding a dependsOn entry. Which expression must be used for originHostHeader?
spiegazione: Correct: reference(variables('webAppName')).hostNames[0]. The reference and list* functions implicitly declare that one resource depends on another, but Learn adds a critical qualifier: "To enforce an implicit dependency, refer to the resource by name, not resource ID. If you pass the resource ID into the reference or list functions, an implicit reference isn't created." Passing the bare name creates the implicit dependency and returns the runtime state of the web app. Why the others are wrong: (b) is syntactically valid and returns the same host name, but because the resource ID is passed into reference() instead of the name, no implicit dependency is created and the endpoint could be deployed before the web app exists. This is the key distinction being tested. (c) resourceId is a pure string-construction function evaluated at compile time. It never contacts the resource provider, never returns runtime state, and creates no dependency at all; it also returns an ID, not a host name. (d) returns the variable's literal string value, not the web app's host name, and creates no dependency.

sotto_argomento: Deploy a resource by using an ARM template or Bicep file
domanda: A DevOps pipeline deploys a root ARM template that includes a linked template through a Microsoft.Resources/deployments resource. To clean up resources that are no longer defined, an engineer sets "mode": "Complete" in the properties of the linked deployment resource. Which statement correctly describes the outcome?
opzione_a: The linked deployment deletes any resource in the resource group that is not defined in the linked template.
opzione_b: Complete mode is supported only for root-level templates; for linked or nested templates you must use incremental mode.
opzione_c: The linked deployment deletes resources that are not defined in the linked template across every resource group in the subscription.
opzione_d: Complete mode works in a linked template only when the template uses the subscriptionDeploymentTemplate.json schema.
spiegazione: Correct: Complete mode is supported only for root-level templates. Learn states: "Only root-level templates support the complete deployment mode. For linked or nested templates, you must use incremental mode." The mode set on a nested deployment resource cannot be Complete. Why the others are wrong: (a) describes what the engineer intends, but the platform does not honour complete mode at the nested level, so no cleanup deletion occurs from the linked deployment. (c) is wrong on two counts: complete mode never spans a whole subscription, and when a template deploys to more than one resource group only resources in the resource group named in the deployment operation are eligible for deletion; resources in secondary resource groups aren't deleted. (d) inverts the facts. Subscription-level deployments don't support complete mode at all, so the subscription schema would make complete mode less available, not more. Microsoft's current guidance is to use deployment stacks when deletions are required, as complete mode is being gradually deprecated.
tags: arm template,complete mode,linked template,nested template,deployment modes

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
domanda: You are editing an ARM template and must build the resource ID of an authorization rule named auth1, which belongs to a queue named queue1, inside a Service Bus namespace named namespace1. All resources are in the current subscription and resource group. Which expression returns the correct resource ID?
spiegazione: Correct: resourceId with one name argument per type segment. The syntax is resourceId([subscriptionId], [resourceGroupName], resourceType, resourceName1, [resourceName2], ...). Learn instructs: "To get the resource ID for a child resource, pay attention to the number of segments in the resource type. Provide a resource name for each segment of the resource type," and gives this exact pattern as its example. The type has three segments (namespaces/queues/authorizationRules), so three name arguments are required. Why the others are wrong: (a) passes a single slash-delimited string as one name argument. The number of name arguments must match the number of type segments; they are not concatenated into one parameter. (c) uses the parent type Microsoft.ServiceBus/namespaces, which has only one segment, and then supplies three names. The type and the name count do not match, and the type does not identify an authorization rule. (d) subscriptionResourceId is for resources deployed at subscription level, such as policy assignments or role definitions. A Service Bus authorization rule lives in a resource group, so resourceId is the correct function.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Deploy a resource by using an ARM template or Bicep file
domanda: An administrator intends to decommission several resources in a resource group named RG-Legacy by deploying a trimmed-down ARM template in complete mode. The deployment reports success, but every resource that was expected to be removed still exists. The template is a root-level template deployed at resource group scope, and the resources in question all support complete mode deletion. What is the most likely cause?
opzione_a: A CanNotDelete lock is applied to the resource group.
opzione_b: The administrator was assigned the Contributor role instead of the Owner role at the resource group scope.
opzione_c: The template's contentVersion value was not incremented before the deployment.
opzione_d: An Azure Policy assignment with the Deny effect is applied to the resource group.
spiegazione: Correct: A CanNotDelete lock on the resource group. Learn states directly: "If the resource group is locked, complete mode doesn't delete the resources." The deployment still succeeds for the resources defined in the template, which matches the observed behaviour of a successful deployment with no deletions. Why the others are wrong: (b) Contributor grants full management access to resources including delete permissions; it only withholds the ability to grant RBAC access and manage assignments. Insufficient permissions would also surface as a failed or unauthorized deployment, not a silent success. (c) contentVersion is free-form documentation metadata. Resource Manager does not compare it between deployments and never changes behaviour based on it. (d) A Deny policy assignment blocks the creation or update of non-compliant resources; it does not prevent deletion, and a policy denial would cause the deployment to fail rather than report success. Microsoft recommends running the what-if operation before any complete mode deployment to preview exactly which resources will be deleted.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Deploy a resource by using an ARM template or Bicep file
domanda: Which of the following statements accurately describe incremental deployment mode for ARM templates and Bicep files? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_a: Resources that exist in the resource group but aren't specified in the template are left unchanged.
opzione_b: When an existing resource is redeployed, properties that aren't included in the template are reset to their default values.
opzione_c: It is the mode that Resource Manager uses when no mode is specified on the deployment operation.
opzione_d: Resources that exist in the resource group but aren't specified in the template are deleted.
opzione_e: Changing the location of an existing resource in the template relocates that resource during redeployment.
spiegazione: Correct answers: a, b and c. (a) Learn states that in incremental mode "Resource Manager leaves unchanged resources that exist in the resource group but aren't specified in the template." (b) "When redeploying an existing resource in incremental mode, all properties are reapplied. The properties aren't incrementally added... Properties that aren't included in the template are reset to the default values." The resource definition always contains the final state of the resource and cannot express a partial update. (c) "The default mode is incremental." Why the others are wrong: (d) describes complete mode, not incremental mode. This is the defining difference between the two modes and the most common confusion on this topic. (e) is false. For both modes, "If you try to update the location or type of an existing resource, the deployment fails with an error." You must instead deploy a new resource with the location or type that you need.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Deploy a resource by using an ARM template or Bicep file
domanda: Your organization is documenting the constraints of complete deployment mode before allowing its use in production pipelines. Which statements about complete mode are correct? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_a: Subscription-level deployments don't support complete mode.
opzione_b: Only root-level templates support complete mode; linked and nested templates must use incremental mode.
opzione_c: Complete mode can be selected when deploying a custom template from the Azure portal.
opzione_d: If the target resource group is locked, complete mode doesn't delete the resources.
opzione_e: In a template that deploys to more than one resource group, resources in the secondary resource groups are also eligible for deletion.
spiegazione: Correct answers: a, b and d. (a) Learn states: "Subscription level deployments don't support complete mode." Complete mode applies only at resource group scope. (b) "Only root-level templates support the complete deployment mode. For linked or nested templates, you must use incremental mode." (d) "If the resource group is locked, complete mode doesn't delete the resources." Why the others are wrong: (c) is false. Learn states "Currently, the portal doesn't support complete mode." You must use Azure PowerShell (-Mode Complete), Azure CLI (--mode Complete) or the REST API. (e) is false and inverts the documented rule: "If you deploy to more than one resource group in a template, resources in the resource group specified in the deployment operation are eligible to be deleted. Resources in the secondary resource groups aren't deleted." Note that Microsoft now recommends deployment stacks for deletion scenarios, since complete mode is being gradually deprecated.
tags: arm template,complete mode,deployment modes,resource lock,portal,subscription deployment

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Interpret an ARM template or Bicep file
domanda: A junior engineer is learning to read Bicep files and asks you to confirm the purpose of several language elements. Select the correct answer for each statement.
opzione_a: Keyword used to declare a value that is supplied when the deployment runs: [param | var | output]
opzione_b: Keyword used to declare a value that is calculated inside the file to simplify a complex expression: [param | var | resource]
opzione_c: Decorator that marks a value so it isn't saved to the deployment history or logged: [@description | @secure | @allowed]
opzione_d: Keyword used to reuse code from another Bicep file within the current deployment: [resource | module | output]
spiegazione: Correct selections: param, var, @secure, module. (a) param declares parameters, which Learn describes as values "that need to vary for different deployments" and that can be supplied at deployment time, optionally with a default value (for example, param storageSKU string = 'Standard_LRS'). output returns values from the deployment rather than accepting them. (b) var declares a variable: "To make your Bicep file more readable, encapsulate complex expressions in a variable" (for example, var uniqueStorageName = '${storagePrefix}${uniqueString(resourceGroup().id)}'). resource declares a resource to deploy, not a computed value. (c) The @secure decorator "Marks the parameter as secure. The value for a secure parameter isn't saved to the deployment history and isn't logged." @description supplies documentation text only and has no security effect, and @allowed restricts a parameter to a set of predefined values but does not hide it. (d) module links to another Bicep file so its resources are deployed as part of the current deployment. resource declares a single resource inline, and output returns a value after deployment.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Interpret an ARM template or Bicep file
domanda: Your team is authoring a minimal ARM JSON template and needs to know which top-level elements must be present. For each element, select whether it is required or optional in an ARM template.
spiegazione: Correct selections: Required, Required, Optional, Required. Per the ARM template structure reference: $schema is Required and specifies the location of the JSON schema file that describes the version of the template language (for resource group deployments in Visual Studio Code, https://schema.management.azure.com/schemas/2019-04-01/deploymentTemplate.json#). contentVersion is Required; you can provide any value such as 1.0.0.0 and use it to document significant changes to your template. parameters is Optional; it holds values provided when the deployment is executed, and a template that hardcodes everything needs no parameters. resources is Required; it defines the resource types that are deployed or updated. The other top-level elements (languageVersion, apiProfile, definitions, variables, functions and outputs) are all optional as well, which is why parameters being optional is easy to get wrong when you assume every element you commonly see must be mandatory.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Interpret an ARM template or Bicep file
domanda: Before splitting a very large ARM template into linked templates, an architect reviews the documented limits for a single template. Select the correct limit for each template section.
opzione_a: Maximum number of parameters in a template: [64 | 256 | 800]
opzione_b: Maximum number of variables in a template: [64 | 256 | 800]
opzione_c: Maximum number of resources in a template: [64 | 256 | 800]
opzione_d: Maximum number of outputs in a template: [64 | 256 | 800]
spiegazione: Correct selections: 256, 256, 800, 64. The ARM template structure and syntax reference states each of these limits explicitly: "You're limited to 256 parameters in a template. You can reduce the number of parameters by using objects that contain multiple properties." "You're limited to 256 variables in a template." "You're limited to 800 resources in a template." "You're limited to 64 outputs in a template." The distractors are the real limits from the neighbouring sections, so mixing them up is the realistic failure mode: answering 800 for parameters or 256 for outputs are both plausible-sounding but wrong. Note that the 800-resource limit is per template and can be worked around with linked or nested templates and copy loops, and that using an object parameter is Microsoft's documented technique for staying under the 256-parameter cap.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Deploy a resource by using an ARM template or Bicep file
domanda: Resource group RG1 contains a storage account named storage1, a virtual network named vnet1, and a virtual machine named vm1. An ARM template named Template1 defines only two resources: storage1, with a different SKU than the one currently deployed, and a network interface named nic1 that does not yet exist. Template1 is deployed to RG1. Evaluate whether each of the following statements is true. 1) If Template1 is deployed by using incremental mode, vnet1 is deleted from RG1. 2) If Template1 is deployed by using complete mode, vm1 is deleted from RG1. 3) If Template1 is deployed by using incremental mode, nic1 is created in RG1.
opzione_a: If Template1 is deployed by using incremental mode, vnet1 is deleted from RG1.
opzione_b: If Template1 is deployed by using complete mode, vm1 is deleted from RG1.
opzione_c: If Template1 is deployed by using incremental mode, nic1 is created in RG1.
spiegazione: Statement 1 - No. In incremental mode, "Resource Manager leaves unchanged resources that exist in the resource group but aren't specified in the template." vnet1 is not in Template1, so incremental mode leaves it untouched. Deletion of resources absent from the template is the behaviour of complete mode, not incremental mode. Statement 2 - Yes. In complete mode, "Resource Manager deletes resources that exist in the resource group but aren't specified in the template." vm1 exists in RG1 and is not defined in Template1, so it is deleted. Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines is a parent resource type, and parent resources are automatically deleted when not in a template deployed in complete mode. Statement 3 - Yes. "For both modes, Resource Manager tries to create all resources specified in the template." Incremental mode adds resources that are in the template to the resource group, so nic1 is created. Incremental never means "only update, never create." Note also that storage1 would be updated to the new SKU in either mode, since changing a SKU is a property change rather than a change of location or type.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Interpret an ARM template or Bicep file
domanda: A Bicep file declares a storage account with the symbolic name storage. It also declares a file service resource of type Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/fileServices that sets parent: storage, and a separate resource that reads exampleDnsZone.properties.nameServers from a DNS zone declared in the same file. Evaluate whether each of the following statements is true. 1) The file service resource must include an explicit dependsOn entry that targets the storage account so that it is deployed after the storage account. 2) The resource that reads exampleDnsZone.properties.nameServers has an implicit dependency on the DNS zone. 3) Resources in the file that have no dependency relationship with each other are deployed in parallel.
opzione_a: The file service resource must include an explicit dependsOn entry that targets the storage account so that it is deployed after the storage account.
opzione_b: The resource that reads exampleDnsZone.properties.nameServers has an implicit dependency on the DNS zone.
opzione_c: Resources in the file that have no dependency relationship with each other are deployed in parallel.
spiegazione: Statement 1 - No. In Bicep, "A resource that includes the parent property has an implicit dependency on the parent resource." The parent: storage assignment is enough to guarantee ordering, and Learn is explicit that "When an implicit dependency exists, don't add an explicit dependency." This is a genuine difference from ARM JSON, where "An implicit deployment dependency isn't automatically created between a child resource and the parent resource" and dependsOn must be set. Statement 2 - Yes. "An implicit dependency is created when one resource declaration references another resource in the same deployment." Reading a property through the symbolic name exampleDnsZone creates that dependency automatically, with no dependsOn required. Statement 3 - Yes. "Azure Resource Manager evaluates the dependencies between resources, and deploys them in their dependent order. When resources aren't dependent on each other, Resource Manager deploys them in parallel." This is why Learn warns that setting unnecessary dependencies slows deployment time.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Interpret an ARM template or Bicep file
domanda: An ARM template deploys four resources into a single resource group. The template defines the following dependsOn relationships: vm1 depends on nic1; nic1 depends on vnet1; vnet1 depends on nsg1; and nsg1 declares no dependencies. Arrange the four resources in the order in which Azure Resource Manager deploys them, from first to last.
spiegazione: Correct order: nsg1, vnet1, nic1, vm1. "Azure Resource Manager evaluates the dependencies between resources, and deploys them in their dependent order." The dependsOn element "enables you to define one resource as a dependent on one or more resources," and a resource is deployed only after everything listed in its dependsOn array has been deployed. Resolving the chain: nsg1 has no dependencies, so it is deployed first. vnet1 depends on nsg1, so it follows. nic1 depends on vnet1, so it is third. vm1 depends on nic1, so it is last. Because this is a linear chain rather than a set of independent branches, no two resources can be deployed in parallel here; if the dependencies were removed, Resource Manager would deploy the independent resources concurrently. Note that Resource Manager identifies circular dependencies during template validation, so a chain that looped back on itself would fail validation before any resource was deployed.
